title: Can two physical devices transfer and reconstruct the smallest useful knowledge chain?
hypothesis: A receiver on a second physical machine can reconstruct the same current claim and history from a relation-free append-only chain sent by yukabox.

contract.author_id: logical pocket i that owns this history
contract.chain_id: one history owned by that pocket i
contract.previous_revision_id: null for the first record; otherwise its direct parent
contract.claim: what the pocket i believed at this revision
contract.evidence_id: pointer to the separately checked evidence capsule
contract.active: false only when the latest record withdraws the claim

ordering_rule: Parent links define order. Timestamps do not choose the current revision.
same_chain_rule: All records must have the same author_id and chain_id, and every non-root parent must exist in the received payload.
current_rule: The only record that is not named as another record's parent is current. Two such records mean forked; none means invalid.
transport: SSH carries the frozen JSON in this development test. SSH is not proposed as the final Pocket i relay protocol.
claim_boundary: Locked physical development test. It can prove exact transport and reconstruction across two machines. It cannot prove cryptographic identity, hostile-peer resistance, internet-scale routing, source truth, privacy, or the final relay design.
